about: The nineteen faces this format ships, as files, so a reel renders the same on every machine and nothing is fetched at build time. All SIL Open Font License, licence text beside each file. Chosen from what short form actually uses in 2026 (Montserrat, Poppins, Anton and Bebas are the four a viewer has already scrolled past a hundred times) plus the current design faces (Bricolage, Geist) and the one this format was measured on (Zen Dots).
law: One face carries the whole reel: captions, the opening, the big words, the end card, the names under logos and every card heading change together. Mono code, chart figures and the serif inside a document replica keep their own, because they imitate a real thing.
measured: cap, size, fits: sizePx is the font size that gives this format's 62 px cap height, read from the face's own cap height. fitsSentence and fitsUpper are how many characters of one real sentence fit inside the caption's maximum width of 0.77 of a 1080 frame at that size, so a face that fits fewer characters is a face that puts fewer words on a page. Every face in this file is measured the same way, so the numbers compare.

families.workhorse: what most reels use; safe, and safe is often right
families.loud: condensed or very heavy; more words per line, more shouting
families.current: what design led accounts are using now
families.heading: for light cards, never for captions over footage
families.signature: the face of the reels this format was measured on

fonts.name: Montserrat ExtraBold
fonts.is: wide geometric capitals and a tall lowercase, even stroke
fonts.use: The default of short form. If nothing about the account says otherwise, this is the safe pick: it is what most reels a viewer has already scrolled past were set in, so it reads as a video rather than as a design.
fonts.avoid: when the account wants to look unlike everyone else

fonts.name: Poppins Bold
fonts.is: perfect circles, tall lowercase, no sharp corners
fonts.use: The friendly one. Lifestyle, coaching, health, anything where the voice is warm. It softens a hard claim, which is the reason to use it and the reason not to.
fonts.avoid: a technical account, where it reads as marketing

fonts.name: Inter Black
fonts.use: The one that says nothing of its own. Use it when the pictures are doing the talking and the words should be furniture, or over a busy room where a face with personality turns into noise.
fonts.avoid: when the reel is all captions and no pictures; it has nothing to carry them

fonts.name: Archivo Black
fonts.is: heavy neutral grotesque, tight and square
fonts.use: Weight without style. The most solid choice on a light or busy background, because the strokes are thick enough that the shadow never has to work.
fonts.avoid: long lines: it fits the fewest characters of the neutral faces

fonts.name: Anton
fonts.is: condensed, ultra bold, one weight only
fonts.use: The loudest face per pixel. Thirty characters fit on a line where Montserrat fits eighteen, so it is the answer when the speaker talks fast and the captions run long. Fitness, motivation, anything shouted.
fonts.avoid: a calm delivery: it makes an even voice sound like an advert

fonts.name: Bebas Neue
fonts.is: tall condensed capitals, no lowercase at all
fonts.use: High energy and clean. Good for one or two word pages where each page is a beat, and for a title line held above the head.
fonts.avoid: sentence case, which it cannot do, and long lines, which turn into a wall

fonts.name: League Spartan Black
fonts.is: geometric, very heavy, wide round shapes
fonts.use: Between Montserrat and Anton: heavier than the workhorses, wider than the condensed ones. It looks deliberate rather than default, which is the reason to reach for it.
fonts.avoid: small text of any kind; it only works big

fonts.name: Bricolage Grotesque ExtraBold
fonts.is: a grotesque with odd, slightly irregular corners
fonts.use: The most installed new face of the last two years, and the current answer to looking made rather than generated. Design, product, craft, anything where the account is the taste.
fonts.avoid: an account whose audience has never seen it; it reads as a choice, and a choice has to be earned

fonts.name: Geist Black
fonts.is: the contemporary technical default, plain with a sharper edge than Inter
fonts.use: For developer and product accounts. It is what the tools those viewers use every day are set in, so it reads as native to the subject.
fonts.avoid: a lifestyle account, where it reads as cold

fonts.name: Space Grotesk Bold
fonts.is: technical with odd corners and a mechanical rhythm
fonts.use: A technical account that wants a face with an opinion. Pairs with terminal and code cards without imitating them.

fonts.name: Instrument Serif
fonts.is: editorial display serif, sharp, high contrast
fonts.use: Headings on light cards, and the accent word inside the paper dress. It is the reason the paper dress reads as a printed page.
fonts.avoid: captions over footage: it is too fine to survive a shadow on a moving picture

fonts.name: Zen Dots
fonts.use: The face of the reels this format was measured on. It fits twelve characters a line in capitals, which forces one or two words a page, which is what makes that look read the way it does.
fonts.avoid: long lines and any account that wants to look like everyone else

fonts.name: Unbounded ExtraBold
fonts.is: very heavy, wide, square shapes with rounded corners
fonts.use: The loud contemporary display face. It fills the frame and looks designed on purpose, which is what most talking head reels are missing.
fonts.avoid: long captions: fifteen letters a line is not many

fonts.name: Boldonse
fonts.is: enormous capitals on a small body, blocky and tight
fonts.use: More words per line than anything else with this much weight. Reads as a printed poster rather than as a caption.
fonts.avoid: a calm delivery, and any clip where the room behind is already busy

fonts.name: Russo One
fonts.is: heavy square grotesque, one weight only
fonts.use: Weight with no personality of its own. The most legible loud face of the ten, and the safest over a busy room.
fonts.avoid: when the account wants to look unlike everyone else

fonts.name: Krona One
fonts.is: wide, heavy, generously spaced, one weight only
fonts.use: Editorial. It slows the reading down, which suits a considered delivery and a light card.
fonts.avoid: fast talkers: it fits the fewest letters of the ten

fonts.name: Orbitron Black
fonts.is: geometric, technical, wide, drawn on a grid
fonts.use: Technical accounts. Reads as machinery rather than as marketing, which is the reason to use it and the reason not to.
fonts.avoid: anything warm, personal or spoken softly

fonts.name: Big Shoulders Display ExtraBold
fonts.is: condensed, heavy, tall, drawn for signs
fonts.use: The most letters per line of the ten. The answer when the speaker talks fast and the captions run long.
fonts.avoid: a slow, quiet clip, where it shouts over an even voice

fonts.name: Chakra Petch Bold
fonts.is: semi condensed with cut corners and a mechanical rhythm
fonts.use: Technical without being cold. It fits a lot on a line and still has a shape of its own.
fonts.avoid: an editorial or lifestyle account, where the cut corners read as a game

boardIs: The ten the setup page offers, in this order. Every one of them was picked off the type board this format's own reels were chosen from, and every one of them carries a caption over footage at 62 px cap without a shadow having to work. The other nine faces stay in the pack because a buyer may name one, and because a replica of a real thing keeps its own face; they are not on the page.
another: A buyer may name any face on fonts.google.com instead. The setup page loads it live to show it on their own frames; the build needs the file, so the agent downloads it into workspace/library/fonts/ before rendering.
